title: Sheaf Hom from a finitely presented module into a quasi-coherent module is quasi-coherent
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal G$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation](2) and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then the sheaf Hom $\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom], with sections $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_W}(\mathcal G|_W,\mathcal F|_W)$ over an open $W\subseteq X$, is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module.

source.place: Schemes, Section 01LA (label section-quasi-coherent, line 4717), item (10), which refers to Modules, Lemma 01CQ (modules-lemma-internal-hom-locally-kernel-direct-sum) and item (5) (kernels of maps of quasi-coherent modules); cited as 'Schemes, Section 01LA' in the proof of Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01YB

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$. By [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation](2), choose an open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$, integers $m,n\ge0$, and $a:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}$ with cokernel map $b:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal G|_U$ (composing the chosen cokernel with its isomorphism to $\mathcal G|_U$). By [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits](2), $\mathcal F|_U$ is quasi-coherent. For every open $W\subseteq U$, part (1) of that same node preserves the cokernel diagram, so $b|_W$ is a cokernel of $a|_W$. The free modules restrict to $\mathcal O_W^{\oplus m}$ and $\mathcal O_W^{\oplus n}$: their sections and restrictions are the same componentwise ones on opens contained in $W$.

source.place: Modules 01CQ, lemma-internal-hom-locally-kernel-direct-sum, first assertion, using its local finite presentation

proof.text: Put $\mathcal E=\mathcal F|_U$. Every finite sum $\mathcal E^{\oplus r}$ is quasi-coherent: for $r=0$, the zero module is the sectionwise kernel of $\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal E}$, hence quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel]; for $r+1$, its sectionwise decomposition $\mathcal E^{\oplus(r+1)}=\mathcal E^{\oplus r}\oplus\mathcal E$ and [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-direct-sum] give the induction step. In particular both the $n$-fold and $m$-fold sums are quasi-coherent, including zero ranks.

Write $a(e_k)=\sum_{i=1}^n a_{ik}e_i$, with $a_{ik}\in\mathcal O_X(U)$, and define the morphism $A:\mathcal E^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal E^{\oplus m}$ on an open $W\subseteq U$ by $A_W((s_i))=(\sum_i a_{ik}|_W s_i)_k$. It is linear and commutes with restriction by this formula. An $\mathcal O_W$-linear morphism $\chi:\mathcal O_W^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F|_W$ is uniquely determined by $s_i=\chi_W(e_i)$, by [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. It annihilates $a|_W$ exactly when $A_W((s_i))=0$. Since $b|_W$ is a cokernel, such a $\chi$ factors uniquely as $\psi\circ b|_W$, where $\psi:\mathcal G|_W\to\mathcal F|_W$. Thus $\psi\mapsto(\psi_W(b_W(e_i)))_i$ is a linear bijection from $\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)(W)$ to $\ker A_W$. Its formula commutes with restriction; the inverse does too by uniqueness of factorization. Hence [def-pur-sheaf-hom] identifies the restriction of the Hom sheaf to $U$ with the sectionwise kernel $\ker A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel] and Step 2 this kernel is quasi-coherent.

source.place: Modules 01CQ, lemma-internal-hom-locally-kernel-direct-sum, first assertion (finite presentation calculation); Schemes 01LA, item (10)

proof.text: For the arbitrary point $x$, quasi-coherence of the Hom sheaf on $U$ supplies an affine neighbourhood $V\subseteq U$ of $x$ on which it is $\widetilde M$ for a module $M$, by [pqf-def-coherent]. Since $U$ is open in $X$, $V$ is also an affine open neighbourhood in $X$ and the restriction of the original Hom sheaf to $V$ is the same sheaf. Every $x$ therefore has the affine neighbourhood required by [pqf-def-coherent], proving the claim.
